title: Virtual environments and pip

spans.text: A virtual environment isolates each project's package versions so updating one project does not accidentally break another.
venv isolates dependencies per project. Create and activate an environment, install packages through that interpreter's pip, and record requirements in a requirements file.
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
python -m venv .venv
python -m pip install requests
python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt
Creates .venv, installs the package, and writes installed versions to requirements.txt; command output varies.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Calling pip as `python -m pip` reduces the risk of installing into the wrong interpreter.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Share setup instructions and dependency files, not the .venv directory itself.

spans.title: Why it matters
spans.text: A virtual environment isolates each project's package versions so updating one project does not accidentally break another.
Keep the interpreter, pip, and project packages in the same virtual environment.
